title: On Generalized Token Graphs
summary: The vertices of a $k$-token graph of a graph $G$ correspond to $k$ indistinguishable tokens placed on $k$ different vertices of $G$. Changing some conditions on both the nature of the tokens and the number of tokens allowed in each vertex of $G$, we define a generalization of token graphs, which we call generalized token graphs or simply supertoken graphs, which have different applications.
